summary: Backend-only regression + new-feature verification. All 70 tests PASS (60 previous + 10 new). Verified: (1) Partial PUT /api/settings uses exclude_unset — sending {managerCommissionPct:15} preserves googleApiKey & fcRate. (2) Dashboard math with sale=200, bill=80, drawing=10, commission=20%: grossProfit=120, commission=24, drawings=10, netProfit=86; all required fields present (openingBalance/openingCash/openingInventory/closingBalance/managerCommissionPct/commission/netProfit/periodStart). (3) GET /api/reports/pnl now returns commission + managerCommissionPct, netProfit = grossProfit - commission - drawings. (4) POST /api/periods/close creates a snapshot in db.periods with every required summary field, creates an inventoryChecks record with actualStock=500, bumps settings.currentPeriodStart to today+1, sets openingInventory=500 and openingCash=<previous cash>. GET /api/periods returns the new period. (5) Post-close dashboard: totalSales=0, totalPurchases=0, openingBalance=openingCash+500, closingBalance=openingBalance. (6) POST /api/reset without confirm → 400; with ?confirm=YES wipes suppliers/bills/sales/payments/inventory/periods, resets accounting settings, but PRESERVES googleApiKey and fcRate. Post-reset dashboard returns zeros. Suppliers-count regression verified.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1116 lines — approaching the 700-line split threshold. Consider splitting into routers (settings.py, suppliers.py, bills.py, sales.py, payments.py, inventory.py, periods.py, ai.py, reports.py, admin.py) for maintainability.
close_period() computes closing_cash from dashboard()['cash'], which already includes opening_cash — correct, but worth an inline comment because it's a common off-by-one trap.
reset endpoint uses query-string confirm=YES. Consider also supporting header/body confirm to reduce accidental URL logging exposure (not a bug, security nit).

GEMINI_MODEL='gemini-3.5-flash' is unusual — verify this model name is intended and current for Google GenAI; typical names are gemini-2.5-flash or gemini-2.0-flash. Not tested here (out of scope), noting for awareness.
seed_data_creation: Each test class does its own reset + reseed with TEST_-prefixed data. Final teardown resets DB and clears the seeded googleApiKey so downstream test modules (TestMissingKeyReturns401) continue to see 'no key' state. No residual data left.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Full backend regression suite lives in /app/backend/tests/ and is orchestrated by pytest with junitxml -> /app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_results.xml. Key endpoints exercised by the new suite: PUT /api/settings (partial), GET /api/dashboard (new fields commission/netProfit/openingBalance/closingBalance/periodStart), GET /api/reports/pnl (now includes commission & managerCommissionPct), POST /api/periods/close (ClosePeriodIn: actualStock, notes), GET /api/periods, POST /api/reset?confirm=YES (400 without confirm; preserves googleApiKey+fcRate). IMPORTANT: /api/reset preserves googleApiKey by design — any test suite that assumes no key must explicitly clear settings.googleApiKey via PUT /api/settings {googleApiKey:''} in its setup.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bugs found. During the first run 4/70 tests failed (TestMissingKeyReturns401::*) because my module-scoped fixture seeded googleApiKey='TEST_KEY_PRESERVE' and the reset-teardown correctly preserved it per new spec, leaking a valid-looking key to downstream modules. Fixed the fixture to explicitly clear googleApiKey after reset. Root cause was test-fixture bleed, not a product bug.
